summary: The note describes the Argo-class, a pair of coastal submarines built in 1936 by Cantieri Riuniti dell'Adriatico in Monfalcone for Portugal. Portugal could not pay the construction costs, so the Royal Italian Navy operated the boats instead. Both served in the Mediterranean at the start of the Second World War, moved to the BETASOM base at Bordeaux in 1940, returned to the Mediterranean in 1941, and were sunk within days of the September 1943 Italian armistice.
one_line: The Argo-class was a two-boat class of coastal submarines built in 1936 for Portugal and operated by the Royal Italian Navy.
key_facts: The Argo-class was a class of two coastal submarines.
The Argo-class submarines were built by Cantieri Riuniti dell'Adriatico in Monfalcone.
The submarines were built for Portugal.
Portugal was unable to pay the construction costs of the Argo-class submarines.
The Royal Italian Navy operated the Argo-class submarines after Portugal could not pay construction costs.
The Argo-class submarines were built in 1936.
Both Argo-class submarines served in the Mediterranean Sea at the start of the Second World War.
In 1940 the Argo-class boats were transferred to the BETASOM Atlantic submarine base at Bordeaux.
The Argo-class boats returned to the Mediterranean in 1941.
Both Argo-class submarines were sunk within a few days of the September 1943 Italian armistice.
